- **self**: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads (18/5)

## Definitions

- [statement] A compute maximum is not an absolute cost ceiling: storage auto-scaling can raise the maximum tier to accommodate disk capacity and disable downward scaling. Review disk allocation and downward-scaling settings after a storage-driven tier increase. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-storage.md · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads
- [statement] Rolling resizing is not a guarantee of unchanged latency. MongoDB documents primary elections, retryable writes, reduced secondary availability, and possible initial-sync load during migrations; Mydbops recommends a rollback plan and validation for production resizing. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/scale-cluster.md · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads · also: https://www.mydbops.com/blog/how-to-reduce-mongodb-atlas-costs-at-scale

## How it works

- [statement] For predictable batch windows, scheduled Triggers can raise capacity before demand and lower it afterwards; Hyperflow describes this pattern in production. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/scheduled-triggers-tutorial.md · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads · also: https://medium.com/@kelhike/cutting-mongodb-atlas-costs-how-we-reduced-our-bill-by-over-40-2036a3c4f2b9
- [statement] Atlas Core downscales one tier within its minimum bound. It requires no downscale or provisioning/unpause in 24 hours and no node restart in 12 hours; evaluation starts when downscaling is enabled. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-core.md · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads
- [statement] Reactive scale-down also requires no manual or automatic downscale or provisioning/unpause within 24 hours and no node stop/restart within 12 hours. Evaluation starts when downscaling is enabled. These gates mean a finished batch does not imply an immediate tier reduction. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-core.md · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads
- [statement] For predictable batch windows, schedule an API-driven tier increase before the batch and a decrease afterwards. MongoDB documents scheduled Triggers for this pattern and warns that reactive scaling may miss sudden bulk-insert spikes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/scheduled-triggers-tutorial.md · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-core.md
- [statement] Choose the post-batch tier from several weeks of utilization, including peak CPU, memory, cache, IOPS and connections. Change one tier at a time, observe the following cycle, and keep a rollback path; average idle CPU alone is insufficient justification. (medium confidence) — https://www.pointfive.co/efficiency-hub/inefficiencies/overprovisioned-mongodb-atlas-cluster-tier · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads · also: https://www.mydbops.com/blog/how-to-reduce-mongodb-atlas-costs-at-scale

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Enable downward compute scaling and set a minimum tier below the current tier; a minimum pinned to the current tier prevents automatic savings during quiet periods. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-core.md · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads · also: https://www.pointfive.co/efficiency-hub/inefficiencies/overprovisioned-mongodb-atlas-cluster-tier
- [statement] Check connection limits before downsizing: Mydbops warns that smaller tiers have lower connection caps and unbounded application pools can cause too-many-connections errors after a resize. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-07) — https://www.mydbops.com/blog/how-to-reduce-mongodb-atlas-costs-at-scale · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Operational-node downscale eligibility requires CPU below 45%, current WiredTiger cache below 90%, and projected lower-tier memory below 60%, over both 10-minute and four-hour windows. Low displayed system memory alone does not establish eligibility. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-core.md · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads
- [statement] AWS's July 2026 worked example reports approximately 30% lower monthly volume costs by scheduling gp3 performance around nightly reconciliation and morning peaks. It concerns a self-managed database, so it does not establish an Atlas savings percentage or Atlas controls. (low confidence) — https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/storage/optimize-amazon-ebs-volume-performance-the-right-amount-at-the-right-time/ · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads
- [statement] For Atlas Core operational nodes, reactive downscaling requires CPU below 45%, current WiredTiger cache usage below 90%, and projected memory on the lower tier below 60%, each across both 10-minute and 4-hour windows. Every node must qualify. M10/M20 CPU thresholds are relative to instance baseline CPU. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-core.md · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Hyperflow's June 2025 account reports over 40% Atlas cost reduction from a combination of scheduled scaling, driver compression and tuning. Its example scales M40 during business hours and M20 off-hours; the total cannot be attributed to scale-down alone. (low confidence) — https://medium.com/@kelhike/cutting-mongodb-atlas-costs-how-we-reduced-our-bill-by-over-40-2036a3c4f2b9 · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads
- [statement] Atlas Core storage auto-scaling only grows disks. If the proposed smaller compute tier cannot support current disk capacity or provisioned IOPS, Atlas blocks the downscale and may raise the minimum tier or disable downward scaling. Reducing batch data does not automatically reverse provisioned storage growth. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-storage.md · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Planning inference: model the actual high-capacity duration, including provisioning lead time and delayed downscale, rather than equating it with batch runtime. Atlas eligibility windows and AWS's best-effort modification timing both support including this overhead. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-core.md · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads · also: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/storage/optimize-amazon-ebs-volume-performance-the-right-amount-at-the-right-time/
- [statement] Planning inference: estimate the compute benefit from time actually spent at the smaller tier, rather than batch duration alone. PointFive describes per-node hourly tier billing, and MongoDB documents scheduled up/down resizing; compare the two tier configurations across all billed data-bearing nodes. (medium confidence) — https://www.pointfive.co/efficiency-hub/inefficiencies/overprovisioned-mongodb-atlas-cluster-tier · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/scheduled-triggers-tutorial.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Right-size from several weeks of representative CPU, memory, cache and connection measurements, then reduce a tier at a time and re-measure. Mydbops specifically warns that lower connection limits can expose oversized pools. (medium confidence) — https://www.pointfive.co/efficiency-hub/inefficiencies/overprovisioned-mongodb-atlas-cluster-tier · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads · also: https://www.mydbops.com/blog/how-to-reduce-mongodb-atlas-costs-at-scale
- [statement] A February 2024 user report describes an M20 downscale followed by a CPU alert and an M30 upscale roughly 76 minutes later. The author suspects startup CPU; the thread does not establish causality or current behavior. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/cpu-measurement-after-autoscaling/265524 · keywords: Scale-down tuning for spiky batch workloads
